# Changelog fixture

Verbatim sections of CHANGELOG.md (as of the 0.157.6 release) used by test_release_notes.py.

## [Unreleased]

## [0.157.6] - 2026-10-22

### Fixed

- **Only `FIPS=1` builds an image with the FIPS 140 module: the default images were built with it too (#685).** `Dockerfile.logs` and `Dockerfile.traces` set `ENV GOFIPS140=${FIPS:+v1.0.0}` after `ARG FIPS=0`, and in `${VAR:+word}` a variable set to `0` still counts as set, so the default `lakehouse-logs` and `lakehouse-traces` images and the `-fips` images were the same binary (`GOFIPS140=v1.0.0-c2097c7c`, `-tags=fips140v1.0`, `DefaultGODEBUG=fips140=on`). Both Dockerfiles now export `GOFIPS140=v1.0.0` in the build step only when `FIPS` equals `1`, so the default images use Go's standard crypto and `fips-status` reports `disabled`, as documented; the `-fips` images are built with the same settings as before (the new `-fips` `lakehouse-logs` binary is byte-identical to the one the old default build produced). The default images change as a result: their crypto is the standard library instead of the FIPS 140-3 module (the binary is 0.3-0.5 % larger, measured on linux/arm64; `fips140=on` is no longer the built-in default), and operators who relied on the default image being FIPS must switch to the `-fips` tag. `scripts/ci/tests/test_fips_build_arg.py` fails if a Dockerfile selects the module with anything other than an exact `"$FIPS" = "1"` comparison, and the `trivy-image` jobs now run `scripts/ci/check_fips_variant.sh` (`go version -m`) and `fips-status` on the image built for each of the four release variants.

### Security

- **The base images of the release Dockerfiles are pinned by digest (the shipped image contents are unchanged; no change to image versions or runtime behaviour).** `Dockerfile.logs`, `Dockerfile.traces` and `Dockerfile.datagen` now read `image:tag@sha256:<digest>` on every `FROM` line, for the distroless runtime base and for the Go builder image (the digest of the multi-arch index, so linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 both resolve), and keep their human-readable tags. The Go image of the parity compose file is pinned the same way, and the temporary entries for these files are removed from `scripts/ci/image_pins_allowlist.txt`.

- **The parity ratchet holds one pass floor per signal, and a skipped parity test now fails the run (CI and test tooling only; no change to the Lakehouse binaries or to runtime behaviour).** `scripts/ci/parity_ratchet.py` read one combined `min-pass` floor, so a whole signal's unlocked results (all logs results, or all traces results) could skip or disappear while the job stayed green. `tests/parity/known_failures.txt` now also holds `min-pass-logs` and `min-pass-traces`, set to the lowest pass count of the last five green runs on `main` (669 logs results, 418 traces results, 1192 in total), and the ratchet fails when a signal falls below its floor or reports no result at all; a result belongs to a signal by the name rules of `signal_of`, and a unit test fails for any `tests/parity` test that no rule names. A test that reports `skip` fails the run unless the allowlist lists it as `# expected-skip: <test>  # <reason>`; an entry whose test stops skipping is stale. The registry gate holds the new floors as it holds `min-pass` (they only go up) and fails a PR that adds an expected skip. The 19 places in the traces parity tests that skipped when the hot or the cold tier returned nothing (14 in `coldhot_endpoint_parity_test.go`, 4 in `traces_parity_test.go`, 1 in `servicegraph_parity_test.go`) now wait up to 30 seconds for the data and then fail with the evidence; no assertion was weakened. The parity summary and the PR quality report print logs and traces results side by side.

- **The registry gate recognises digest pins on the base images of the release Dockerfiles (CI only; no change to the Lakehouse binaries or to runtime behaviour).** `scripts/ci/pr_classify.py` and its Go twin in `tests/conformance/registry` now accept an optional `@sha256:` digest (exactly 64 lowercase hex characters) after the tag of the Go builder image, so a toolchain bump can move the tag and the digest together and a build container in the parity stack can be pinned. A change to the `FROM` lines of `Dockerfile`, `Dockerfile.logs` or `Dockerfile.traces` that only adds, removes or changes the digest of an image, with the image name, tag, platform and stage name equal, is no longer classed as a product change. Everything else in those files, a digest without a tag and any malformed digest still are. The shared fixture gains the accepted and rejected cases for both twins.

- **The external-reader test matrix uses a patched release of a transitive Python dependency (test tooling only; no change to the Lakehouse binaries or to runtime behaviour).** `thrift` moves from 0.16.0 to 0.24.0 in `tests/readers/requirements.txt`, which closes Dependabot alerts 29, 30 and 31. `parquet-tools` pins `thrift` below 0.17, so it is now installed from its own hashed file, `tests/readers/requirements-parquet-tools.txt`, after the main lock and without dependency resolution; its other dependencies are listed in `requirements.in`. Only the `readers-inprocess` job installs it.

- **The vulnerability scan can now fail the build, and the release images are scanned (CI only; no change to the Lakehouse binaries or to runtime behaviour).** The required `trivy` check scans the repository for fixable HIGH and CRITICAL vulnerabilities (and for secrets) and exits non-zero on a finding; before, it could only report. The vulnerability database is downloaded in a step of its own (`scripts/ci/trivy_fetch_db.sh`: three mirrors, three rounds, the cached copy as a last resort), so a registry or network problem is reported as such and is never mistaken for a finding. New `trivy-image-logs`, `trivy-image-logs-fips`, `trivy-image-traces` and `trivy-image-traces-fips` jobs build the release images from the repository Dockerfiles with the release build arguments (nothing is pushed) and apply the same policy to each, and `trivy-gate-fixture` shows on every run that the scan fails on a fixture with a known fixable vulnerability and passes on a clean one. Exceptions go in a reviewed `.trivyignore`, one reason and one expiry date per entry. `scripts/ci/tests/test_trivy_gate.py` fails if a trivy step loses its exit code, severity or fixed-only policy, if a scan runs without the separate database step, or if a release image is no longer scanned.

## [0.157.5] - 2026-10-21

## [0.157.4] - 2026-10-21

### Security

- **Every GitHub Actions workflow pins its actions to a full commit SHA, and a new `workflow-lint` check lints the workflow files (CI only, no runtime change).** All 171 action references that used a tag or branch now name a 40-character commit with the version as a trailing comment, expressions that were interpolated into `run:` scripts in the fuzz, load-test, badges and MinIO image workflows are passed through `env:`, and `.github/workflows/workflow-lint.yaml` runs actionlint and zizmor (pinned, checksum-verified) on every pull request and push to `main`, with the findings that exist today listed in `.github/zizmor.yml`. CodeQL also analyses the workflow files now (`Analyze (actions)`), and `scripts/ci/tests/test_workflow_action_pins.py` fails if an action reference is added without a SHA pin and version comment.

- **Tools installed in CI are pinned to exact versions and their downloads are verified (CI only, no runtime change).** `govulncheck`, `gosec` (and the `x/tools` it is built with) are installed at exact versions instead of `@latest`, the `gitleaks` archive is checked against a pinned SHA-256 before it is unpacked, and every `pip install` in the workflows reads a hashed lock file (`--require-hashes`, generated from a `requirements.in` next to it with `pip-compile --generate-hashes`) in place of unpinned or version-only requirements. `scripts/ci/tests/test_ci_tool_pins.py` fails if a moving tool ref, an unverified download, a pipe into a shell, an unhashed `pip install` or an `npm install` is added; the few exceptions are listed, each with its reason, in `scripts/ci/tool_pins_allowlist.txt`.

- **Container images used by the test stacks and CI are pinned by digest (CI and test tooling only; no change to image versions or runtime behaviour).** The images of the Compose stacks, the S3 compatibility job, the MinIO build Dockerfiles and the benchmark, proof and reader stacks now read `image:tag@sha256:<digest>` (the digest of the multi-arch index, so linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 both resolve) and keep their human-readable tag. A new static test, `scripts/ci/tests/test_image_digest_pins.py`, fails when a Dockerfile `FROM`, a Compose `image:` or a workflow container image has no digest; the few references that cannot carry one (images built in the same stack, build-arg bases, the release Dockerfiles until their follow-up change, the Go builder image) are listed with a reason in `scripts/ci/image_pins_allowlist.txt`, and a stale entry fails the test.

- **Dependabot now keeps every dependency ecosystem in the repository updated (CI and test tooling only; no change to any dependency version or to runtime behaviour).** `.github/dependabot.yml` gains `pip` (the hashed requirements locks, including the workflow linter's), `npm` (the documentation site and the Playwright proof project), `docker` (the deployment, MinIO build and S3 compatibility directories) and `docker-compose` (the benchmark, parity and external-reader stacks) entries next to the existing Go modules, GitHub Actions and root Dockerfile entries. Every entry runs weekly, waits 7 days before it proposes a new release, and groups minor and patch updates into one pull request per ecosystem; images this repository builds itself, the VictoriaLogs and VictoriaTraces pins and the test backend that the S3 compatibility job also pins are not proposed. `scripts/ci/tests/test_dependabot_coverage.py` fails when a tracked manifest directory has no matching entry or an entry has no schedule or cooldown, and the exceptions are listed with their reason in `scripts/ci/dependabot_allowlist.txt`. The `dependabot-cooldown` baseline entry is removed from `.github/zizmor.yml`.

- **The changelog gate no longer asks for an entry on Dependabot pull requests that only bump dependency files of the tooling and test trees (CI only; no change to any dependency version or to runtime behaviour).** `changelog-check` skips a pull request only when all of these hold: the event's author is `dependabot[bot]` and the head branch lives in this repository (not a fork), so a branch name, title or commit author cannot claim it; every changed file is modified, not added, deleted or renamed; and every file is a requirements file or hashed lock, a `package.json` or `package-lock.json` under `website/` or `tests/`, a Dockerfile or Compose file under `deployment/`, `scripts/` or `tests/` (including the S3 compatibility stacks), or a workflow in which only SHA-pinned `uses:` lines change. Anything else a Dependabot pull request touches (the Go modules, the release Dockerfiles `Dockerfile.logs`, `Dockerfile.traces` and `Dockerfile.datagen`, `charts/`, `cmd/`, `internal/`, `lakehouse-traces/`, `patches/`, `CHANGELOG.md`) keeps the existing rules, and the check fails closed when the author, the repository or the diff cannot be read. The gate script reads the author and repositories from the workflow's environment instead of interpolating them into the script, and `scripts/ci/tests/test_check_changelog_pr.py` covers the exempt cases, the human and spoofed-author cases and every file class that stays required.

## [0.157.3] - 2026-10-21

## [0.157.2] - 2026-10-21

### Changed

- **Deletes: a tombstone is a write-once object that every pod reads from the bucket.** The definition (and, for a `hide` delete that is undone, an `.undo` object) is created once with `If-None-Match` under `{prefix}_tombstones/`; every pod lists new keys each minute and enforces them, so a delete reaches all pods within a minute instead of at the next restart, and nothing a pod holds locally ever causes a DELETE. While `delete.enabled` is true, a pod that cannot refresh its list for three minutes answers cold and buffer-bridge reads with `503` (an undecodable definition closes only the tenants it names), and a select pod is ready only after its first sync. Only a `hide` delete can be un-deleted; `permanent` and `auto` hide the rows like `hide` and answer `409` to an un-delete, because physical removal is not enabled in this release (#627); `delete.default_mode` now defaults to `hide` (it was `auto`), also for upstream's `run_task`: the bytes stay until retention and direct Parquet readers still see them. `active_tasks` is `[]` and `stop_task` a no-op, as for a finished upstream task. Key times are pod clocks (late keys are counted: `LakehouseTombstoneClockSkew`). New: `lakehouse_delete_tombstone_view_age_seconds`, `LakehouseTombstoneViewStale`, `LakehouseTombstoneUnreadable`. See `docs/deletion-strategy.md`.

### Removed

- **The mutable tombstone protocol and everything built on it:** the per-tombstone record, its disk and S3 write-through, the delete rewriter and scheduler, the leftovers API (`GET /delete/logsql/leftovers`, `/delete/tracessql/leftovers`), their metrics and alerts, and the unread knobs `delete.auto_rewrite_classes`, `delete.rewrite_delay`, `delete.rewrite_max_concurrent`, `delete.verify_interval`. **Upgrade note: tombstones written by an earlier release (`_tombstones/<id>.json`) no longer hide rows and are not migrated; they are rejected without error and counted each hour in `lakehouse_delete_tombstone_keys_rejected_total`. Re-issue those deletes, and remove the old objects by hand.**

### Fixed

- **The compacted layer of the all-column sort parity case no longer leaves an object unmerged (tests only, no behaviour change, #636).** The forced compaction merges only the objects the segment guard releases when it runs, and the case triggered it as soon as two objects per tenant were released; a batch that a segment seal cut into two segments left its later object at L0, which failed the layer proof and the restart layer after it. The case now waits until the guard releases every object of its tenants and requires the trigger to merge them all, and it writes its second batch in two segments on every run, for both binaries.

- **The span events and links parity cases no longer wait up to 12 minutes for the next hour (tests only, no behaviour change).** From minute 48 of an hour, `TestParity_Traces_EventsLinksLayers` and `TestParity_Traces_EventsLinksInvalidUTF8` slept until the next hour before writing their spans, so that a run never crossed an hour boundary. The span time is now the current time, moved by at most 2 s so that every timestamp of a case (span starts and ends, trace index rows, the second batch) falls in one hour partition; this also closes a first-second-of-the-hour window in which the old rule split a case over two partitions. The rest of the case already derives its partition from the span time, and its layer proofs are unchanged.

### Security

- **Go 1.27.3, which fixes GO-2026-6809 (`crypto/x509`) that govulncheck reports.** Go 1.27.2 ships a `crypto/x509` that trusts compromised intermediate certificates, and govulncheck finds it reachable from the S3 client paths (for example `manifest.Manifest.LoadFrom`). Both go.mod files, `go.work`, the three Dockerfiles and the parity runner image now use Go 1.27.3. `govulncheck` reports no vulnerabilities in either module. No source change; Parquet data is unchanged.

## [0.157.1] - 2026-10-19

### Changed

- **The existing lint findings of the parity and chaos test helpers are cleared (tests only, no behaviour change).** Seven findings in `tests/parity` and `tests/e2e` (unchecked `Body.Close` and `json.Unmarshal` results, a redundant nil check, and the complexity of `TestParity_CrossValidation`, whose two sum-per-label subtests now share one helper) no longer fail the lint step's only-new-issues pass on a very large PR, which treats every existing finding of a package as new when it cannot fetch the PR's patch.

- **A tombstone only turns the metadata fast paths off for the files it can match, and a file that must be read is matched per block (both binaries).** A tombstone used to switch off, for every file of the window, the manifest-answered counts, the label-count push-down, the metadata-only row-group reads and the field-value aggregates, and to add its fields to every read; every row of every read file was then matched against every overlapping tombstone through a fresh map, so the cost grew with the number of tombstones. Now a file is read as if there were no tombstone when its own metadata proves, from memory only (no S3 read), that no tombstone acting on its tenant can match a row of it: its time range, a complete manifest label set, or the pmeta bloom for an exact `field:="v"` / `field:in(...)` term on a registered column. Anything undecided (regex, NOT, OR, empty value, prefix, map attribute, unknown bounds, no pmeta) keeps the old path, so every answer is unchanged. The label set of a compaction output is never used (recognised by its level or its `compacted-` key): compaction unions its inputs' sets, which is partial when an input had none (#621). In-process, 8 objects, upstream-shaped tombstones at K = 1, 10 and 100, against main (medians of 6 interleaved runs, every answer equal): with tombstones no file holds, `stats by (service.name) count()` 7.9, 16.4 and 109.7 ms become 5.1, 5.0 and 4.8 ms with 0 object reads instead of 8; with a map-attribute tombstone nothing is provable and the per-block matcher alone takes `field_names` from 21.7, 45.4 and 295.5 ms to 15.6, 16.8 and 24.0 ms; with no tombstone nothing moves. `count()` and hits are answered from the manifest only for a request that carries the timestamp-only hint, which no served handler sets today; the count push-down, the field-value aggregates and every scan do not need it. New section "Per-file gating of a delete" in `docs/read-path.md`.

## [0.157.0] - 2026-10-19

### Changed

- **Reads cut at the retention horizon: a query no longer plans a file that is past its retention, even before the eviction loop has deleted it.** One `retention.Policy` object (tenant overrides and rules included) now serves both the eviction loop and the read path, and it follows upstream VictoriaLogs/VictoriaTraces' day rule for a TTL of a day or more: a file is past its retention once the UTC day of its newest row is before the day of `now - TTL`, so nothing is hidden or deleted up to 23 hours early; a TTL below a day (a Lakehouse extension) stays exact. Every role cuts, so a select pod, which does not run the eviction loop, no longer serves data past its retention. Results change only for data older than its retention that eviction has not yet removed; there is no extra S3 request. Not cut: buffered (unflushed) rows, the tenant list and the stats and admin APIs (a tenant whose only files are past retention stays listed until eviction runs, #619). Raising a retention makes files that were hidden but not yet deleted visible again, and an alias-keyed tenant retention that resolves after start applies to the cut and to eviction alike only after a restart.
